newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees 1997 social security gap near $6 bln.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees 1997 social security gap near $6 bln.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz said on Thursday the deficit in the social security system may balloon to nearly 1,000 trillion lira ($6.13 billion) in 1997.

"To meet the deficit of social security organisations 530 trillion lira was set aside. Estimates show that at the end of the year it will pass 800 trillion lira and may near 1,000 trillion lira," Yilmaz said.
Speaking at the annual general meeting of the Social Security Institution, Yilmaz said the inability of revenues to meet expenditure made it essential to reform the institution.
He said it was necessary to record unregistered employment as part of the reforms.
The chronic deficits in the social security system are a significant factor in the overall financial problems faced by the six-week-old government under Yilmaz.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in a strongly-worded statement on Tuesday that a reform of the system would be needed as part of any stabilisation effort.

The Social Security Institution, which is at the centre of the social security system, is expected to show a deficit of 378 trillion lira in 1996 compared to a deficit of 144.3 trillion lira a year earlier. The comparative figure is not adjusted for annual inflation of around 80 percent.
